messages:
Maya: FYI found a deprovisioned principal still making GETs against redwood-prod-inference S3 bucket after SCIM deprov. SCIM event delivered 2026-03-21T02:14:07Z, API calls at 2026-03-21T02:20:12Z. Can someone triage group-sync -> session path?
Ravi: Which credential was used? user session or service token? Any request ids?
Maya: user session (U-8432). Auth log: 
``
2026-03-21T02:20:12Z request_id=rid-9a3c user=U-8432 token=*** handler=generate_presigned_url bucket=redwood-prod-inference
```
We have webhook success at 02:14:07 and reconcile ran at 02:16:00 and marked deprov, but verifier still accepted session.
Jon: My first guess: rbac role cache TTL + delta-sync optimization. We recently set role_cache TTL to 10m and introduced delta updates that might skip eviction on certain payload shapes.
Sophia: I hit something similar with a group rename where key names changed and cache keys didn't map; which cache are you checking?
Jon: redis key roles:principal:U-8432 existed with TTL 4m at event time. Looks like the reconcile didn't evict the key because delta update path only touches principals listed in change_set.principals, but the webhook used externalId instead of principal_id and mapping failed.
Maya: Also saw a transient KMS decrypt error around the same request: "kms:Decrypt failed key=kms-prod-1 request=rid-9a3c" then a retry succeeded. Could that cause verifier to accept stale sessions?
Ravi: Yes. Our verifier uses the KMS-wrapped signing key; on decrypt failure we fall back to a locally cached verifier key to avoid downtime. That fallback validates signature but doesn't re-check user-state (we only check state at issuance or via revocation list). If a stale session exists and revert to cached public key, it will pass signature checks.
Ashley: So root cause: deprov -> SCIM ok -> reconcile marks disabled -> but existing session still valid (12h TTL) and verifier fallback path accepted it because revocation hook never populated session_revocations.
Maya: Confirmed session_issued_at=2026-03-21T01:50:10Z. Session TTL 12h.
Sophia: Why didn't revocation hook fire?
Jon: Repro: SCIM webhook payload uses externalId=EXT-8432. Provisioner maps EXT-8432 -> U-8432 for provisioning, but the revoke-hook reads payload.principal_id and falls back to externalId if missing, but due to an earlier refactor the revoke pipeline expected principal_id only. Mapping bug caused it to skip populating session_revocations (redis set sessions:revoked).
Maya: Workaround I did: manually added U-8432 to sessions:revoked and flushed roles:principal:U-8432 cache. Access stopped immediately.
Ravi: Proposed short-term mitigations:
- Force a run to invalidate sessions for any principals touched by recent deprov batches (oncall script)
- Disable KMS decrypt fallback (fail-closed) until we can ensure revocation path is reliable
- Add an alert if reconcile marks deprov but sessions:revoked count does not increase for that principal within 1m
Jon: I'll file ENGSEC ticket with triage, logs, and repro. Owners: Jon (fix pipeline), Sophia (mapping), Ravi (KMS fallback config), Maya (postmortem).
security-bot: Incident created: ENGSEC-4321 | SCIM deprov -> retained sessions via verifier fallback
oncall-bot: Emergency runbook scheduled 2026-03-21T03:10:00Z assigned to @Jon @Ravi
Ashley: Long-term proposals:
- Revoke sessions atomically as part of deprovision pipeline (make revoke an integral step of SCIM reconcile)
- Change verifier to consult a lightweight user-state cache updated by SCIM events on every verification (cheap check)
- Add e2e test: SCIM deprov -> revoke -> request denied
Maya: Customer impact: one internal service account pulled a handful of objects. No PII. We'll notify infra owners and export audit logs for the objects accessed.
Ravi: I'll push a short patch to disable KMS fallback in staging and create a config toggle for prod. ETA ~2h.
Jon: ENGSEC-4321 created with labels [scim,deprov,rbac,kms,fallback]. Attached commands/logs used for triage.
Maya: Thanks — manual revocation done and we'll drive follow-up postmortem. :thumbsup:
